title: Crosses of the Tash-Khauli palace, Khiva
subtitle: Tash-Khauli palace, Khiva

construction.note: The finished design was read from Brian Wichmann’s R241B drawing, the centre lines of its bands snapped to exact values: every line lies on a grid of sixths of OA. We devised the construction: the line from K2 to A marks a half and a third, and the rest follows from them. The drawing gives no steps.
construction.changes: The compass steps, their order and the named points are ours. The comparison with the drawing checks the finished lines, not how the design was first laid out. Wichmann draws the lines as bands; the tutorial draws their centre lines. No photo of the palace was checked.

credits.source: Tiling Search, data185/R241B: Khiva majolica, Palace of Tash-Khauli
credits.creator: Brian Wichmann
credits.note: The design was read from his drawing. He takes it from Lazar Rempel, Arkhitekturnyi ornament Uzbekistana (Tashkent, 1961), figure 241, item 2, page 474 (majolica of the Tash-Khauli palace, Khiva), and lists photos of the same design at the Pahlavan Mahmud necropolis in Khiva. The construction is ours.

given.A: Halfway from O to the next cross of the same kind.

steps.text: Draw a horizontal straight line through O and A. Draw a circle with centre O through A.

Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through each of A and B. Draw a horizontal line through each of C and D. These lines make the square cell, with corners K1, K2, K3 and K4. Draw a straight line through O and K1.
steps.textWithoutHelpers: Draw a vertical line through O. The two lines cross the circle at A, B, C and D. Draw a vertical line through A. Draw a horizontal line through C. They cross at K1, a corner of the cell. Draw a straight line through O and K1.

steps.text: Draw a straight line through K2 and A. It crosses the vertical line at M. It crosses the line from O to K1 at T. Draw a horizontal line through M. Draw a line through T at 90° to the line from O to K1.
Draw a circle with centre T through O. It crosses the line from O to K1 at U. Draw a line through U at 90° to the line from O to K1.
The horizontal line through M crosses the line through T at E. It crosses the line through U at G. Draw a vertical line through each of E and G.
Turn the five lines of the last three steps round O by 90°, three times.
Join K1, K2, K3 and K4 to mark the tile that repeats.

ink.text: Ink the cross at O and the lines round it. They close the squares, the ten-sided pieces, and the pentagons round each corner of the cell.

pattern.text: Put copies of the square cell side by side. A cross sits at every centre, and a square with four pentagons round it at every corner.
